page: Amazon Web Services t3a.small is a burstable general-purpose virtual instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and operates using an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The hardware configuration exposes 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core across 2 threads. System memory totals 2.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, and baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the low-footprint performance tier of the burstable allocation model. In synthetic CPU assessments, the t3a.small achieved a PassMark CPU score of 1862.31, with PassMark encryption reaching 1608.29 and memory operations scoring 846.47. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests produced scores of 590.59 and 590.79 respectively. Memory throughput benchmarks recorded 20.84 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 12.35 GB/sec for large block writes. In application benchmarks, the instance delivered 1.26 million Redis SET operations per second, 1.59 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and small 135M LLM prompt processing speeds of 41.1 tokens per second.

The operational profile of the t3a.small emphasizes cost efficiency for intermittent compute patterns via shared-core burstable CPU credits. Because resources are bounded by a single physical core and 2.0 GB of total RAM, sustained intensive computation quickly exhausts CPU burst allocations and risks memory starvation. The instance is suited for lightweight workloads with irregular usage patterns, including small test environments, low-traffic web applications, minimal automation scripts, and background worker queues.
